data.command: What security tools do you have deployed?

data.text:
We've got a mix of tools to keep our system safe and secure. We're running Ubuntu 22.04.3 LTS, with the kernel version 5.15.0-91. Our firewall rules are managed by UFW (Uncomplicated Firewall) on port 22 (SSH) and 80 (HTTP) is allowed for our web server, while 443 (HTTPS) is restricted to only our internal network.

We're using fail2ban for monitoring and blocking brute-force attacks on our SSH server. It's configured to ban IP addresses that try to log in with the wrong password more than 3 times in 1 minute. We're also running a custom set of security scripts that check for suspicious login attempts and system modifications every hour. 

Our web server, running nginx/1.24.0, has a custom configuration that uses the "http" module for serving static files, and the "server_tokens" module is disabled to prevent server identification leaks. We're also using the "geoip" module to block known malicious IP addresses.

As for network traffic analysis, we have Snort running in inline mode on port 162 for log aggregation. It's configured to analyze incoming traffic and alert us on any suspicious activity.
